title: Myt1l and Phf21a perturbations converge on Rreb1-positive mature-neuron remodeling
exact_observed_result: Myt1l loss produced a recurrent mixed program with broad Rreb1 induction and a narrower Kifc2/Slc22a17 down arm, while Phf21a targeting also induced Rreb1 in overlapping thalamic, midbrain, and other neuronal subclasses.
biological_interpretation: MYT1L and PHF21A perturbations may share a noncanonical Rreb1-positive chromatin response in mature neurons, separate from proneural bHLH or motor/pancreatic developmental transcription-factor programs.

support.evidence_summary: Myt1l:F001/F005 and Phf21a:F001 support broad Myt1l and Phf21a Rreb1 induction with weaker whole-signature convergence.

caveats: Myt1l-Phf21a convergence is marker-level; same-cell whole-signature correlations were only about 0.15-0.20.
PHF21A mRNA depletion was not directly detected, so the Rreb1 response needs orthogonal edit validation.

prior_expectation.summary: Myt1l:F001/F005 and Phf21a:F001 support broad Myt1l and Phf21a Rreb1 induction with weaker whole-signature convergence.
